label: Table A2
caption: Table A2 Requirements that apply to material changes of use
description:
The table is titled “Table A2 Requirements that apply to material changes of use”. It is a grid. The left-hand column is headed “Requirement (from Schedule 1 to the Building Regulations 2010)”. The remaining columns are under the grouped heading “Material change of use under:” and are sub-headed “All cases”, “5(a)”, “5(b)”, “5(c)”, “5(d)”, “5(e)”, “5(f)”, “5(g)”, “5(h)”, “5(i)”, “5(j)” and “5(k)”.

The body of the grid uses only one visible marking symbol: a black tick, ✓. There is no printed key, no cross, no filled or empty circle, and no drawing. A tick in a cell shows that the requirement named in that row is marked against the material change of use named in that column. A cell with no tick is not marked, apart from the light blue table ruling. The table has light blue shading in the title and header area and light blue grid lines, but no meaning is given to that shading.

The row-by-row markings are:

A1–A3: ticks in “5(c)”, “5(d)”, “5(e)” and “5(f)”.

B1: tick in “All cases”.

B2: tick in “All cases”.

B3: tick in “All cases”.

B4(1): tick in “All cases”, with a small superscript “1” after the tick.

B4(2): tick in “All cases”.

B5: tick in “All cases”.

Reg. 6(3): tick in “5(k)”.

C1(2): ticks in “5(a)”, “5(b)”, “5(c)”, “5(d)”, “5(f)”, “5(g)”, “5(h)” and “5(i)”; the tick in “5(f)” has a small superscript “2” after it.

C2: tick in “5(a)”, with a small superscript “3” after the tick.

C2(c): tick in “All cases”.

E1–E3: ticks in “5(a)”, “5(b)”, “5(c)”, “5(f)”, “5(g)”, “5(h)” and “5(i)”.

E4: tick in “5(e)”, with a small superscript “4” after the tick.

F1: tick in “All cases”.

G1: tick in “All cases”.

G2: ticks in “5(a)” and “5(b)”.

G3(1)–(3): tick in “All cases”.

G3(4): ticks in “5(a)” and “5(b)”.

G4: tick in “All cases”.

G5: tick in “All cases”.

G6: tick in “All cases”.

H1: tick in “All cases”.

H6: tick in “All cases”.

J1–J4: tick in “All cases”.

K1–K6: no tick in any column.

L1: tick in “All cases”.

M1: ticks in “5(c)”, “5(d)”, “5(e)” and “5(i)”.

P1: tick in “All cases” with a small superscript “5” after the tick, and ticks in “5(a)”, “5(b)”, “5(f)” and “5(g)”.

Q1: ticks in “5(a)”, “5(b)” and “5(g)”.

R1: no tick in any column.

Below the grid is a section headed “NOTES:” with six numbered notes. The notes read exactly:

“1. B4(1) applies to buildings over 15m high. It applies to the whole building even if the change of use only applies to a part.

2. Where new residential accommodation is created.

3. Applies to the whole building not just the parts converted to residential use.

4. If the public building after the change contains a school.

5. P1 applies in all cases if the electricity supply is shared with a dwelling.

6. Regulations 7(1) and 7(2) always apply to the above requirements.”

The superscript numbers in the grid refer to notes 1 to 5. Note 6 has no corresponding superscript marker in the grid and states that Regulations 7(1) and 7(2) always apply to the above requirements.
